title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Nuts and Fruits

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad with nuts and fruits is a nutritious dish that combines tender poultry, crunchy nuts (such as walnuts, almonds or cashews) and fresh fruits (apple, grapes, pomegranate). It is often served as a light lunch or appetizer, providing protein, healthy fats, vitamins and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination of poultry and nuts has been used in Mediterranean cuisine since ancient times.
Fruits add sweetness and improve iron absorption from the meat.
Nuts can be swapped for seeds (pumpkin, sunflower) for a nut‑free version.
A turkey‑based version is popular in the United States around holidays, often with cranberries.
The salad can be served cold or slightly warmed if the meat is reheated.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Healthy fats from nuts
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants from fruit
items.content: Apples, grapes, pomegranate and other fruits supply vitamin C, vitamin K and polyphenols that boost immunity.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Nuts and fruit add fiber, promoting regular digestion and satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad provides iron, zinc and magnesium, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: People with nut allergies may experience reactions ranging from mild to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared dressings or marinades can be high in sodium; making the dressing at home helps control it.

items.title: Meat safety
items.content: Chicken and turkey must be fully cooked and cooled promptly; prolonged storage increases bacterial risk.

items.title: Fruit acidity
items.content: Acidic fruits may increase tooth enamel sensitivity; rinsing the mouth after eating is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled or slightly cooled. Cut the poultry into cubes or strips, coarsely chop the nuts, and dice the fruit. Dress with olive oil, lemon juice, mustard or a yogurt‑based vinaigrette. Fresh herbs such as parsley, basil or mint can be added for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Add nuts just before serving to retain crunch. For longer storage, keep the dressing separate to prevent the fruit from becoming soggy.
